justification: Changes what the production DCP monitor does with every newly found council document: it now downloads each one, reads its cover and rejects duplicates and non-DCP documents in dcp_chapter_registry. A wrong verdict silently drops a real new DCP chapter from review, so every unsure case is kept for a person.

pre_impl.existing_data: Measured 2026-10-23 read-only on production: 28 dcp_chapter_registry rows with registration_status='auto_detected' across 5 councils (city_of_sydney 8, canada_bay 7, bayside 7, canterbury_bankstown 4, woollahra 2), the oldest waiting since 2026-05-18. Opening each file by hand: 3 were the very files already served (Bayside DCP 2022 Amendment 2 = row 725; CB chapters 5.1 and 5.2 = rows 316, 317, same sha256), about 20 were guidelines, technical specifications, policies or public domain plans, 2 were DCP chapters not covered (CB 7.7, Canada Bay appendix 3), and 3 had no readable text or no stated kind.
pre_impl.assumption_mismatch: (1) _auto_register_chapter deduplicated by the label slug only, so a served file under another link label was registered as new; it now also checks the address. (2) A commencement-date reader already existed (scripts/extract_dcp_stated_dates.py); its patterns are reused, not rewritten. (3) Its date patterns match amendment-history tables too, so only the cover text before the first contents / amendment-history heading is read.
pre_impl.new_vs_existing: Applied once to production on 2026-10-23 with the user's yes after a dry run (backup data/db_rollback_backups/verifyops_classify_pre_2026-10-23T070149.json): 21 rows rejected (18 not_dcp, 3 duplicate), 5 tagged and left waiting (2 dcp_needs_person, 3 unreadable), 2 Woollahra rows left untouched because their download failed. From the next monitor run every new document is classified the same way.
pre_impl.external_source_error: A failed download leaves the row untouched and is retried next run; a web page served instead of a PDF, or a damaged PDF, is a red verdict kept for a person, never a rejection.
pre_impl.frontend_type: No frontend change. Only registration_status and detected_category of waiting registry rows change; no served row is touched (every UPDATE is guarded by registration_status='auto_detected').
pre_impl.user_failure_mode: If a real new DCP chapter were wrongly rejected as not_dcp, nobody would review it and the site would keep serving the old rules without saying so. That is why not_dcp needs positive evidence on the cover (another document kind named, and no DCP words), and anything else stays waiting and red in the alarm (new_doc_undecided_3d).

falsifiable_check.command: python -m pytest -q -o addopts= tests/test_verifyops_classify.py tests/test_dockerfile_monitors_imports.py ; PYTEST_REAL_DB=1 DATABASE_URL=<pooler url> python -m pytest -m database -o addopts= tests/test_verifyops_classify_real_db.py
falsifiable_check.fails_when: any of the 28 real documents gets a verdict other than the one a person read from its cover, a row is called its own duplicate, an amendment-history date or a second date is read as the commencement, a plan is not in force on its effective day, a failed download is written, a dry run writes, a decided row is overwritten, a waiting tag is downloaded again, or a verdict is not committed
falsifiable_check.observed_red: YES: 15 hand-made mutants applied one at a time. 14 killed first time; the survivor (in_force d <= today -> d < today) got a boundary test and is killed. A second survivor (commit removed) got a commit-count test and is killed. The real-DB tests insert their own waiting rows on production inside one transaction that is rolled back; they kill the pending() filter, the auto_detected guard on the UPDATE and the not_dcp settlement mapping. Sol cross-review 2026-10-23 found 4 real defects, all fixed with tests and killed mutants: two new copies of one file rejected each other; a rejected row at the same address blocked a new document there; lowercasing the path merged different files on case-sensitive servers; a one-council run classified other councils' documents.

functions.name: classify
functions.input: one document (id, url, sha256, first pages' text) and the other registry rows of its council
functions.output: a verdict dict: duplicate (with the matched row id), not_dcp, dcp (with the one effective date or needs_person), or red
functions.if_none: no text or a failed read -> red

functions.name: cover_text
functions.input: the list of page texts read from the first three pages of the PDF
functions.output: page 1 up to the first contents / amendment-history heading, at most 600 characters
functions.if_none: an empty list gives an empty cover, which classify turns into a red verdict

functions.name: classify_pending
functions.input: connection, a url -> bytes fetch, today, dry_run
functions.output: counts per verdict plus retry; writes one guarded UPDATE per document and commits it
functions.if_none: no waiting rows returns an empty dict and nothing is downloaded or written

functions.name: _auto_register_chapter
functions.input: a newly found hub link with its label, its address and the council's hub page
functions.output: skipped when its address is already a registry row of the council
functions.if_none: rows whose council_url is NULL never match, so the link is registered as before

values.if_missing: red verdict, row kept for a person
duplicate check falls back to the address

queries.where_clause: registration_status = 'auto_detected' AND detected_category not dcp_needs_person / unreadable
id = %s AND registration_status = 'auto_detected'; rowcount must be 1 or the run stops
council = %s AND lower(trimmed council_url) = lower(trimmed new url)

break_it.scenario: A new edition's page 1 runs on into its amendment history with an older date
break_it.what_happens: only the cover before the heading is read
break_it.how: cover_text stops at the first contents / amendment-history heading

break_it.scenario: The council serves an HTML error page at the PDF address
break_it.what_happens: the verdict is red and the row stays waiting for a person to decide

break_it.scenario: A guideline is actually adopted as part of the DCP but its cover does not say so
break_it.what_happens: it is rejected as not_dcp and drops out of the review list without a person
break_it.how: only covers that name another kind of document are rejected; the rejection is visible (detected_category not_dcp) and reversible from the backup

break_it.scenario: A cover states two different commencement dates, for example original and amended
break_it.what_happens: no date is chosen; the row stays waiting and needs a person to read it

break_it.scenario: The registry row changed between the read and the write
break_it.what_happens: the run stops with an error instead of overwriting
